Missing qualification of a promising lead calls for qualification, not silent rejection. An infeasible low-J point is not a feasible incumbent.

Feasible designs can still be improved: assess whether service-temperature phase gain, reduced competing phases or an unresolved solute interaction merits another comparison while respecting J. A conditional experiment is a decision commitment, not a permanent search obligation. Missing J/phase data cannot itself refute the value of measuring J/phase. For a cost-reduction experiment, retaining the desired benefit can satisfy its premise; do not change the criterion afterward to require a benefit increase. Keep the qualified incumbent while testing.

When multiple downstream comparisons share a large penalty, check whether the team has considered its upstream origin using the relevant physical diagnostic. If a controlled midpoint retains favorable J and reduces competing-phase cost, check whether stopping leaves a consequential, testable interval unresolved. Ask the planner to resolve that question or state a concrete limit; do not choose samples yourself. Do not assume monotonicity or require every indicator to improve.
